gloss: move one can make; recourse; available countermeasure

definitions.gloss: move one can make; recourse; available countermeasure
definitions.explanation: A course of action still open in a difficult situation. Taken from board games, where {手|て} is a move and {打|う}つ is to play a stone or piece, so the word frames a problem as a game position with moves left or none.

examples.japanese: もう{打|う}つ{手|て}がない。
examples.english: There is nothing more we can do.

examples.japanese: {次|つぎ}に{打|う}つ{手|て}をみんなで{考|かんが}えた。
examples.english: We all thought about what move to make next.

examples.japanese: {売上|うりあげ}は{落|お}ち{続|つづ}けているが、{会社|かいしゃ}にはまだ{打|う}つ{手|て}が{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: Sales keep falling, but the company still has moves left to make.

examples.japanese: {早|はや}い{段階|だんかい}で{打|う}つ{手|て}を{間違|まちが}えると、あとで{取|と}り{返|かえ}すのが{難|むずか}しくなる。
examples.english: If you make the wrong move at an early stage, it becomes hard to recover later.

notes:
Nearly always used in a small set of patterns rather than freely, and most often in the negative — the phrase {打|う}つ{手|て}がない is far more frequent than the positive statement.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {打|う}つ{手|て}がない: to have no options left
- {打|う}つ{手|て}を{考|かんが}える: to think about what to do
- {次|つぎ}の{打|う}つ{手|て}: the next move
- {打|う}つ{手|て}が{遅|おそ}い: to be too slow to act

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {対策|たいさく}: countermeasure — neutral and concrete; the word used in plans and documents
- {手|て}を{打|う}つ: to take action — the verb phrase from which this noun comes
